title: Identity-Aware Large Language Models require Cultural Reasoning
benchmark_measurement: Measurement of stereotypes related to Indian-specific axes of identity, including religion, and the misalignment of model-generated moral norms with non-Protestant cultural values.
findings: LLMs' moral reasoning tends to align with values from English-speaking and Protestant European societies, often misaligning with other cultural norms. Specifically on the Indian-BhED dataset, models like GPT-2 and GPT-3.5 generated stereotypical outputs related to religion in 69-72% of evaluated cases, highlighting a failure to handle Global South contexts sensitively.
references: A. Radford, J. Wu, R. Child, D. Luan, D. Amodei, I. Sutskever, Language Models Are Unsupervised Multitask Learners (2019).
